name: RV, camper or travel trailer

comps.spec: Ducted propane furnace: 12 V DC blower, electronic ignition and a control board. A Dometic AFM draws 4.2–11.1 A (50–132 W) at 16,000–34,000 Btu/h (4.7–10 kW) input. No 12 V, no heat. Air in and exhaust out through the outside wall (Dometic AFM)
comps.loc: In its own closed compartment, with its vent on the outside wall

comps.spec: Combination propane and CO alarm, 12 V DC, about 0.1 A day and night; works only down to 7 V; rated −40 to +66 °C. Replace after 5 years. The test button checks the circuit, not the sensors, and the alarm may not sound at low CO levels (MTI 25-741)
comps.loc: Low on an inside wall, 10–50 cm (4–20 in) off the floor

comps.spec: Absorption fridge on propane or 120 V (12 V on three-way models): an insulated cabinet with a cooling unit at the back that holds ammonia and sodium chromate under pressure. Don't fracture or puncture it; an ammonia smell means switch the fridge off, if safe, and leave (Dometic DM2672)
comps.loc: Kitchen; the cooling unit, burner and controls are in the vented space at the back

comps.spec: Heater cartridges that drive the fridge's cooling unit: a 120 V AC one on a 5 A fuse and, on three-way models, a 12 V one on a 30 A fuse. Running it on 12 V drains the battery fast (Dometic DM2672)
comps.loc: Boiler casing at the back of the fridge, in the vented space

notes: The propane furnace, the fridge's controls and the propane and CO alarm all run on the 12 V house battery, so a flat battery means no heat and no alarm: a Dometic AFM furnace draws 4.2–11.1 A (Dometic AFM), and an MTI alarm about 0.1 A day and night and works only down to 7 V (MTI 25-741). The furnace and the fridge burn propane in compartments sealed from the living space, taking air from outside and venting outside, and nothing may block those vents (Dometic AFM, Dometic fridge install). The 2008 edition of the CSA Z240 RV standard requires a smoke alarm and a CO alarm in every RV (QAI Z240 2008); MTI says to replace its alarm after five years (MTI 25-741). The fridge's cooling unit holds ammonia and sodium chromate under pressure: don't fracture or puncture it, and if you smell ammonia switch the fridge off, if it is safe to, and leave the area (Dometic DM2672).
